passage:
Sunday. First week as head of the fest team. I've swung from one extreme to the other. On Monday I redid Aditi's poster because the font looked off, and she said “oh, okay” in a flat voice. On Wednesday I said nothing when Karan missed the deadline, because I didn't want to be the bossy one. Today the sponsor letter wasn't ready and everyone looked at me. My ears went hot. I realised I'd been trying to prove I could lead instead of asking what the team needed.

Tomorrow: ask everyone what's blocking them, split the letter into two parts, and ask Aditi to explain her font choice.
— Bidisha

qa.q: What did Bidisha redo on Monday?
qa.a: Bidisha redid Aditi's poster because the font looked off.

qa.q: Why did Bidisha say nothing when Karan missed the deadline?
qa.a: Bidisha did not want to be seen as bossy after over-controlling earlier, so avoiding conflict felt safer.

qa.q: What is Bidisha's plan for tomorrow?
qa.a: Bidisha plans to ask everyone what is blocking them, split the sponsor letter into two parts and ask Aditi to explain the font choice.

qa.q: How might Aditi have felt when the poster was redone?
qa.a: Aditi probably felt undervalued and quietly hurt, shown by the flat “oh, okay.”

grounding: A student head of a fest team feels pressure to prove themselves, swings between over-control and avoiding conflict, and refocuses on what the team needs.

passage:
Mahima: hey did you see the schedule? why did you change my slot
Aparna: I moved it, sorry. I wanted the demo to look tight
Mahima: you didn't ask
Aparna: I know. I keep fixing everything myself 😅
Mahima: also last week you said nothing when Dev never sent the banner
Aparna: yeah. I didn't want to sound harsh
Mahima: it's either taking over or going quiet. can you just tell us what the goal is and who owns what?
Aparna: ...that's fair. I'll post the goal tonight. Demo day is what matters, not me looking in charge
Mahima: thank you 🙂 happy to move slots if you explain

qa.q: Why did Aparna say nothing when Dev never sent the banner?
qa.a: Aparna did not want to sound harsh, having taken over earlier and feeling unsure how to lead.

qa.q: What did Aparna decide to post that night?
qa.a: Aparna decided to post the goal that night, after agreeing Mahima's point was fair.

qa.q: How might Mahima have felt when the slot was changed without a word?
qa.a: Mahima probably felt overlooked and frustrated, but was willing to speak plainly and to help once the reasons were shared.

grounding: A student leading a team for the first time swings between taking over and going quiet, and learns to serve the group's goal.
